comments.author: David Hutchison
comments.message:
Thanks for this work, doing anything involving sorting in Liquid is so much more painful than it should be!

I'm running a slightly modified version of this that makes the sorting of tags case insensitive. It is not very efficient but I don't think it can be improved on with the current filters available. Source is at https://github.com/dhutchis... .

comments.author: Aurelio Jargas
comments.message:
Thanks for the excellent post. I really enjoyed your all-in-one tag page.

Testing it locally I've noticed that the "num_words" variable is not necessary, one can use directly the "site.tags.size" property. Or maybe I'm missing something?

{% for item in (0..site.tags.size) %}

replies.author: LanyonM
replies.message: I've tested locally as well and you are correct - the num_words variable is not needed. Thanks for the improvement! I'll update the post in the coming days.

replies.author: LanyonM
replies.message: It took me longer to get to it than intended, but the post (and site) has been updated. Thanks again for the suggestion!

replies.author: Róbert Papp
replies.message: Improving on this, how about {% for tag in tag_words %}? Then tag=tag name, and site.tags[tag]=posts; it looks cleaner.

comments.author: Clint
comments.message: Awesome tip, I have been looking for this for a while.

comments.author: Bruno Pinheiro
comments.message:
This is working for me:

{% assign sorted_tags = (site.tags | sort:0) %}
{% for tags in sorted_tags %}

replies.author: Michael Ransley
replies.message: This did the business for me, thank you for the post and your comment.

comments.author: mDfRg
comments.message:
I can confirm that the syntax:
{% assign sorted_tags = (site.tags | sort:0) %}
{% for tag in sorted_tags %}
<li>{{ tag | first }}</li>
{% endfor %}
works perfect.

Thank you very much Michael!

comments.author: Róbert Papp
comments.message: That capture with | strip_newlines looks paranoid, there's no new line in the creation of tag_words, why do you need to trim it? Even if you do {% assign this_word = tag_words[item] | strip_newlines %} may be simpler.

comments.author: Jingying Zhou
comments.message: thank you! but I ran into a problem that, when I have different collections (say, _posts and _poetry) only tags under _posts were counted

replies.author: Róbert Papp
replies.message:
See https://jekyllrb.com/docs/v... "site.tags.XXX=The list of all Posts with tag XXX.". Notice it says "Posts" not "every document". site.tags is a map from tags to a list of posts.

Check out http://stackoverflow.com/q/... and https://talk.jekyllrb.com/t... for more info on collection tags (a feature not directly supported by Jekyll)

replies.author: Jingying Zhou
replies.message: Thanks Róbert for the links and explanations. It seems that only posts would be counted from site.tags and collection tags should be treated in a different manner.
